newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PAPER SAYS CHILDREN OF METS PLAYER PUT IN FOSTER CARE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PAPER SAYS CHILDREN OF METS PLAYER PUT IN FOSTER CARE.

text.p: The children of New York Mets outfielder Carl Everett reportedly were placed in foster care on Thursday after a Shea Stadium child-care worker noticed bruises on Everett's 5-year-old daughter.

The New York Times reported in Friday's edition that Everett and his wife had been interviewed by police and will not face any charges. The girl and Everett's 4-year-old son eventually will be returned to their parents, authorities told the newspaper.
"We accept their explanation of the incident," said Sgt. Cory Cuneo, a police spokesman.
The causes for the bruises were not disclosed, according to the Times, which said it made unsuccessful attempts to reach Everett.
Mets general manager Steve Phillips held a team meeting to discuss the case before Thursday's victory over Colorado. He also refused to discuss the matter publicly.
"It's a personal matter for the family, and if and when they would like to address it themselves, they can do that," Phillips told the Times. "We support Carl and his family."
Everett did not play in Thursday's game.
"Early this morning, we agreed he should stay home today and take care of family matters," Phillips told the newspaper.
